speaker: Tianyi Lou
title: Property \(P_{\mathrm{naive}}\) for Big Mapping Class Groups
abstract: Mapping class groups of finite-type surfaces are well understood and exhibit rich dynamics. In contrast, mapping class groups of infinite-type surfaces (big mapping class groups) are less explored and often fall outside standard frameworks. Abbott-Dahmani showed that acylindrically hyperbolic groups (without non-trivial finite normal subgroups) satisfy property \(P_{\mathrm{naive}}\). But for an infinite-type surface \(S\), \(\mathrm{Map}(S)\) is not acylindrically hyperbolic, so that result cannot be applied. Assuming that \(S\) contains a nondisplaceable finite-type subsurface, Horbez-Qing-Rafi construct a continuous nonelementary action of \(\mathrm{Map}(S)\) on a hyperbolic quasi-tree of curve graphs. We use this action to prove that \(\mathrm{Map}(S)\) has \(P_{\mathrm{naive}}\) for orientable \(S\) and non-orientable \(S\): for any finite collection of non-trivial elements \(h_1,\dots,h_n\), there exists an infinite-order element \(g\neq 1\) such that \(\langle g,h_i\rangle \cong \langle g\rangle * \langle h_i\rangle\) for all \(i\).

speaker: Xueqing Wen
title: Multiplicativity of the perverse filtration for SL_n Hitchin systems
abstract: The Hitchin fibration equips the cohomology of Higgs bundle moduli spaces with a perverse filtration. The P=W conjecture predicts that this filtration is compatible with cup product, a property that does not hold for general projective morphisms. In this talk, I will present a proof of multiplicativity for the canonical SL_n Hitchin system in arbitrary rank, over a smooth projective complex curve of genus at least two, with fixed determinant of degree coprime to the rank. I will begin by reviewing the Fourier-transform approach of Maulik–Shen–Yin to the perverse filtration for compactified Jacobian fibrations. I will then explain how to adapt this approach to compactified Pryms, highlighting the new ingredients required in the SL_n setting. Two difficulties arise: the dual fibration is naturally a quotient stack, and the Hitchin direct image has contributions supported on proper endoscopic loci. Addressing these requires a Fourier-correspondence formalism for quotient stacks and a comparison between Fourier projectors and the endoscopic correspondence. This comparison replaces the full-support argument in the compactified Jacobian case and identifies the Fourier filtration with the perverse filtration over the elliptic locus of an auxiliary twisted Hitchin system.

speaker: Shihang He
title: Singularity blow up method and positive mass theorem
abstract: The Schoen-Yau minimal hypersurface approach to the positive mass theorem faces difficulties in high dimensions due to the presence of singularities. In this talk, I will introduce a singularity blow-up method that allows us to overcome some of these difficulties. This method leads to a proof of the Riemannian positive mass theorem in dimension 8. By combining it with torical symmetrization and generic regularity theory, we further extend the theorem to dimension 19. This is joint work with Yuguang Shi, Haobin Yu, and joint work with Yuchen Bi, Tianze Hao, Yuguang Shi, and Jintian Zhu.
